notes.title: The demons are both tragic and hot in Possessor(s), the Hyper Light Drifter studio's new fantasy platformer
notes.notes:
Heart Machine’s side-scrolling metroidvania platformer Possessor(s) is Hollow Knight with a splash of Amanita Design’s Creaks. The bulk of your enemies are household objects - vending machines, plant pots, office printers and other fittings that have become vessels for demons. From this premise springs a note of tragedy powerful enough to conquer my outrage at a game title that has brackets in it. The demons are not, in themselves, violent - it’s inhabiting the inanimate that maddens them. “Possessing something cold and dead is agony… so they lash out,” explains Rhem, a mortally wounded devil you meet in the prologue.

notes.title: Possessor(s) Animated Short I: Professor Foss & NEW Gameplay
notes.notes:
[p]Once an absent-minded teaching professor and Luca’s former instructor on campus, Professor Foss is now in the clutches of the Knowledge Demon. In pursuit of ever more information, the demon has grotesquely twisted and torn apart his body. Yet, the Professor appears entirely unaware of the transformation—he remains cheerful and content, seemingly oblivious to his condition and eager to converse with Luca.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="9TakNJBQ7lE;full"][/previewyoutube][p]
In [i]Possessor(s)[/i] you will play as Luca, a high-schooler trapped in the ruins of Sanzu City. Professor Foss was one of her teachers. What is the mysterious research being performed in the basement laboratories of Luca’s old school, and what will Luca and her demon, Rhem, discover when they go to investigate? [/p][p][/p][p]You needn’t wait long to find out! Players can now take their first steps into Sanzu - the crippled city that serves as a backdrop to the game’s events - in the first publicly playable demo, [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3712530/Possessors_Demo/"]available now on Steam[/url]![/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3712530/Possessors_Demo/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: Hyper Light Drifter dev's new game drops this year, but you can try it now
notes.notes:
When it comes to videogames with impeccable vibes, I always think of Heart Machine. Hyper Light Drifter perfectly blends bold pixel art with evocative emptiness in a way that makes that world unforgettable. Solar Ash, meanwhile, transplants that style into a clean-cut 3D environment with some of the best scale I've ever seen. It's safe to say that Heart Machine's next game, Possessors, has caught my eye. If you can't wait either, you'll be glad to hear that there's a demo available today.

notes.title: Possessor(s) Is a Demon-Infused Metroidvania That Bleeds Style
notes.notes:
Every frame of Possessor(s) drips with personality, from demonic potted plants to whip-slinging showdowns. I’ve been a fan of the Metroidvania genre for quite a while now. It’s my go-to for handheld gaming or when I travel, and some of my all-time favourite games sit squarely in that category. But in all my time playing through the genre’s highlights, I never knew I needed more demon-based sex appeal—at least, not until now.

Possessor(s) is a unique experience from the studio that brought us Hyper Light Drifter and is published by Devolver Digital—and it’s fantastic. Set in a world where a disaster has unleashed demons into the city of Sandy, you play as Luca. With the help of the (extremely hot) demon Rhem, you must uncover what happened to your family, escape the city, and fight to survive along the way.

notes.title: Possessor(s) Deep Dive Story Details
notes.notes:
Possessor(s) is a high-speed action side-scroller that fuses platform-fighter precision with intense, high-stakes combat. As Luca, players must master fluid movement, aerial juggles, and the dark powers of Rhem to survive relentless melee encounters against the horrors of Sanzu City.

Sanzu was meant to be the future—a self-sustaining utopia where families could live, work, and thrive under the global megacorp Agradyne. But three years ago, something escaped from Agradyne’s deepest labs. With it came a nightmare: demons desperate for human hosts. Many lost control, mutating into grotesque abominations. In response, Agradyne abandoned the city, sealing the survivors inside a labyrinth of crumbling skyscrapers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051013/a4172b06af609ecccfffaf1f94910b62341ddebb.png[/img]

Luca wakes in the ruins—once an ordinary teenager in a corporate-run town, now fighting to survive. Her only ally is Rhem, a powerful and embittered demon who once endured Agradyne’s experiments. Rhem possesses Luca not to control her, but to keep them both alive. Their uneasy pact is simple: she’ll help Rhem return home, and he’ll help her fight.

Together, they journey through a city haunted by tragic fusions of humans and demons—each an echo of manipulation, desperation, and broken bonds. As they unravel the truth behind Sanzu, Luca will be forced to confront the sinister reality beneath its polished corporate veneer.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051013/7014e423c84d56ec45349bfaff687e3160c71aac.png[/img]

Luca’s arsenal is as unconventional as her battles. Armed with whatever she can find, she carves through demons with kitchen knives, pummels them with a computer mouse, cracks skulls with a hockey stick—or even shreds enemies with a guitar.

Her trusty knives are quick and precise, letting her dash in for rapid strikes before slipping out of danger. Keeping up the pressure staggers enemies, leaving them vulnerable. Juggling foes with directional attacks prolongs their suffering, turning each fight into a brutal display of skill.

But in Sanzu, anything can be possessed—people, vending machines, potted plants… even an Agradyne Series LC65 Multi-Function Printer Scanner. Danger lurks in plain sight, and to bring Rhem home, Luca must challenge the city’s most formidable demons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45051013/7568761be63335ce131b412924f5a3eb24c7ec63.png[/img]

As they grow stronger, Luca and Rhem unlock new combat techniques, traversal abilities, and weapon modifications. Players can customize their combat loadout, assigning each attack button to different weapons for near-limitless combo potential.

Survive. Adapt. Fight back. The horrors of Sanzu City won’t stop—so neither can you.
We can't wait to share more Possessor(s) news with you later this year!
